name: F/A-18E/F Super Hornet
summary: Twin-engine carrier-based multirole fighter, the backbone of US Navy carrier air wings; larger successor to the legacy Hornet.

wings: Mid-mounted trapezoidal wing with a distinct dogtooth notch in the leading edge
Large, broad leading-edge root extensions (LERX) running forward to the cockpit
Underwing pylons splayed (toed) outward; wingtip missile rails
engines: Two engines with round exhausts side by side
Rectangular, angular (caret-style) intakes beneath the LERX
fuselage: Larger, heavier fuselage than the legacy Hornet with a long nose
Bubble canopy; F model has a two-seat tandem cockpit
tail: Twin outward-canted vertical fins set forward of the exhausts

tellTales: Rectangular, angular intakes under big wing-root extensions
Twin outward-canted fins on a carrier fighter with outward-splayed wing pylons
Dogtooth notch in the wing leading edge

confusedWith.howToTell: The Super Hornet is bigger with rectangular intakes, a wing dogtooth and larger LERX; the legacy Hornet has rounded D-shaped intakes and a straight leading edge.
The Super Hornet carries missile rails at the wingtips; the Growler has bulbous wingtip receiver pods and large jamming pods under the wings.
The Super Hornet has two side-by-side exhausts, rectangular intakes and external pylons; the F-35 has one sawtooth exhaust and a clean stealth shape.

usCount.source: FlightGlobal World Air Forces 2026 / US Navy fact file
